newsitem.title: UK: London gold steady, silver tests key $5.00 level.
newsitem.headline: London gold steady, silver tests key $5.00 level.

text.p: Gold was slow and steady on Thursday afternoon, but silver probed the key $5.00 an ounce level following its brisk rally in New York overnight.
Bullion fixed at $381.75 an ounce, compared to $381.60 in the morning and a Wednesday London close of $381.30/$381.80.
"Gold is running into selling at around $382. There's not a lot it can do at this point," a dealer said.

Silver, which trundled up about 10 cents on a New York-led fund rally was made a move on the psychological $5.00 an ounce level. "There's still talk of stops above $5.00 and the trade is looking for a pop up to about $5.03," a dealer said.
Around the fixing the New York Comex December gold contract was ahead by $0.50 at $384.00.
Absent a conspicuous move by the funds to reverse recently established short positions in gold, dealers were focusing on silver which was taking on the $5.00 resistance.
"There was some fresh buying in silver, and the market was short so it ran some stops yesterday," a dealer said.

The move was related to fears about Russian leader Boris Yeltsin's health as well as concern over recent news of declining Comex stocks. The Yeltsin health rumours have been denied at governmental level.
Gold had moved up in sympathy with silver recersing the roles of the past couple of weeks in which gold was setting the tone for the complex.
However now that gold had moved off the floor, it was finding good support just under $380.
"It's off its lows for now after hitting $387," a dealer said.
The dealers' view of silver was mixed, reflected in short selling being absorbed by physical buying, a dealer said.
Dealers said silver could move quickly if it got through $5.00 where buy stops would be triggered between $5.02-$5.04.
Just after the gold fixing silver was probing $5.00 having touched $5.01/$5.03 and was last indicated at $5.00/$5.02.
Platinum was also moving up in sympathy with silver.
It was last seen at $388.30/$389.30 after closing at $384.50/$385.50 on Thursday and moving off its lowest fixing since January, 1994 struck on October 1.
Palladium attracted less sympathy support and was quoted at $117.25/$118.25, $0.75 above the previous close.
